objective: Establish how HolyAgent can use browser-use (github.com/browser-use/browser-use) as the headless browser of the screen capability for Pi specialists, replacing the Playwright MCP server.
scope: Answer from browser-use's own repository, README, docs (docs.browser-use.com) and PyPI metadata, current as of 2026-11:

1. Does browser-use ship an MCP server (for example `uvx browser-use --mcp` or a browser-use[cli] extra)? Exact command, transport (stdio?), the tools it exposes and their names, and which tools need an LLM API key versus drive the browser directly. HolyAgent's specialists are themselves the model, so direct browser tools without a nested agent are wanted; say whether the nested-agent tool can be turned off.

2. Headless operation in a cloud container or CI with no display: flags or environment variables for headless, using an existing Chromium binary (this container has one at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium; Playwright browsers path PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH), whether it installs its own browser (playwright install / patchright), and what it writes to disk (profiles, config, telemetry). How to turn telemetry off (ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY or similar).

3. Requirements: Python version, uv/uvx, the exact latest stable version on PyPI and its license; how an exact version pin is given to uvx (browser-use==X.Y.Z) and whether uvx can be told to use the public index explicitly (like npx --registry) so a project's uv config cannot redirect it.
4. How HolyAgent's dependency updater could move a PyPI pin: the PyPI JSON API endpoint for the latest stable release.
5. Anything that makes it unsuitable for a non-interactive specialist (prompts on first run, API key required at start).

Context: HolyAgent registers MCP servers for Pi in packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts (PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SERVER, npxServerArgs) and pins Pi packages in packages/runtime/src/config/pi-packages.json moved by scripts/dependency-pins.ts (mise run deps:update). Read those files in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-bump to say what would have to change for a PyPI-pinned uvx server, at the level of which pieces, not code.
constraints: Make no edits and no git writes.
Separate sourced facts (with URL) from inference.

result:
result: browser-use 1.0.0 ships a stdio MCP server with direct browser tools and no nested agent, but it attaches to an already-running Chrome and does not launch Chromium itself (the deprecated `--mcp` does). That makes it a poor 1:1 replacement for `@playwright/mcp --headless --isolated`.

blockers: none
questions: none

findings (F = sourced fact, I = inference)

1. MCP server
- F: Config is `command: uvx`, `args: ["--from","browser-use==1.0.0","browser-use","--cli-mcp"]`, a stdio MCP config. [https://docs.browser-use.com/customize/mcp-server]
- F: The tools are `browser_exec(code)` (Python with Browser Harness helpers and raw CDP; the namespace persists), `browser_screenshot(full,max_dim)` and `browser_login(force)`. [same page]
- F: "There is no MCP tool that runs the full browser-use Agent", so no nested LLM. The Playwright-style tool names (`browser_navigate` etc.) are gone. [same page]
- F: No LLM key is needed. `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` is only for Browser Use Cloud browsers. [same page]
- F: The 0.x tools, including `retry_with_browser_use_agent`, now return an error. [same page]
- I: A model's tool surface is one Python-exec tool plus a screenshot tool. `browser_login` opens a browser for approval, so it should be left off or ignored in specialists.

2. Headless and disk
- F: The `--cli-mcp` server drives the Chrome you have open. Local attach needs `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`. [https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/browser-use-cli]
- F: An alternative is `BU_CDP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9222` (or `BU_CDP_WS`) plus `BU_NAME`. Browser-harness install docs: launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=<dir>` ("best for unattended automation"). [https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/skills/browser-harness/references/install.md]
- F: `--mcp` is deprecated. It serves the same three tools "on its own Chromium", with the 0.x domain restrictions read from config.json. [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/browser-use/browser-use/main/browser_use/cli.py]
- F: The library's `Browser('chromium')` is headless when there is no display and takes `executable_path=`. [README, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/browser-use/browser-use/main/README.md]
- F: `browser-use install` runs `uvx playwright install chromium`. It is not needed when a Chrome already exists. [cli.py]
- F: I found no documented env var for the Chromium path or for headless in the MCP path. I do not know whether `--mcp` honors `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` or finds `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`.
- F: Disk: browser-harness state lives under `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/browser-harness` (auth, workspace, sockets, logs, screenshots, temp). `BH_HOME` or `BROWSER_HARNESS_HOME` relocate it. browser-use config is `~/.config/browseruse/config.json`, relocated by `BROWSER_USE_CONFIG_DIR` or `BROWSER_USE_CONFIG_PATH`. [install.md, cli.py]
- F: Telemetry: `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY` turns it off (cli.py). Browser-harness also has `browser-harness telemetry disable`. [install.md]
- I: A local daemon is spawned per `BU_NAME`. The CDP port has no authentication. [README]

3. Requirements and pinning
- F: The latest stable release on PyPI JSON is 1.0.0. The license is MIT (`license_expression`). `requires_python` is `<4.0,>=3.11`. [https://pypi.org/pypi/browser-use/json]
- F: The README on `main` already says 1.0.1. 1.0.1 is not on PyPI as latest, so the sources conflict. Pin from PyPI, not from the README.
- F: Pin form is `--from browser-use==X.Y.Z`. The README says to pin exactly and never use `>=`.
- F: uvx cannot take `--registry`, but `uvx --default-index https://pypi.org/simple` or `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` exists. `uv tool run` ignores project `uv.toml` and `pyproject.toml` and reads only user-level and system-level config. `--no-config` or `UV_NO_CONFIG` skips all config files. [https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/, https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/configuration-files/]
- I: Use `uvx --no-config --default-index https://pypi.org/simple --from browser-use==1.0.0 browser-use --cli-mcp`. This is the PyPI-pinned equivalent of `npxServerArgs`. I did not run it.

4. Updater
- F: `https://pypi.org/pypi/browser-use/json` gives `info.version` as the latest. The `releases` map is also present. I did not check whether `info.version` skips prereleases, so also filter for stable releases.

5. Non-interactive suitability
- F: No API key is needed for local use. The first attach to a user Chrome prompts "Allow remote debugging" (not applicable with `BU_CDP_URL`).
- I: Fit is poor unless HolyAgent launches Chromium itself with `--remote-debugging-port` and sets `BU_CDP_URL`. Alternatively use the deprecated `--mcp`, which may be removed.
- I: The tool name pattern changes from `mcp__playwright__browser_*` to `mcp__browser_use__browser_*`.

HolyAgent changes (read from /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-bump)
- `pi-packages.json` is npm-only and `PiPackageName` keys are npm names. A PyPI pin needs a separate table or a new key kind, plus an `npxServerArgs` analogue (`uvxServerArgs`).
- `scripts/dependency-pins.ts` compares against the npm `latest` dist-tag. It needs a PyPI fetcher (JSON endpoint above) and the equivalent caret-range test (`scripts/dependency-ranges.test.ts`).
- `capabilities.ts`: replace PLAYWRIGHT_* constants and the `tools.screen`/`rootExclude` patterns.
- `capabilities.ts`: the `needs` entries change from `npx`/node to a `uvx` command check, with Python 3.11 handled by uv.
- `capabilities.ts`: `chromiumFlag` has no equivalent. A launcher step for Chromium plus `BU_CDP_URL` is needed.
- Env for the server: `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=0`, plus `BH_HOME` or `BROWSER_USE_CONFIG_DIR` under a temp dir.

notes: Recommend against replacing Playwright MCP unless a Chromium-launch step is acceptable. A decision for the root: dependency and architecture change.
